title: RWB-S7-E6019-APP: the reject reason and the decision code have no field, column or list, R-WO-16's owner conflicts with the FSD role and the permission table, the plan's C row is empty while the step consumes three contracts, DP-04 and DP-09 are absent, and no published row moves a case out of RETURNED_TO_PURSUE
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S7-E6019-APP; context pack S7 rwb-writeoff (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 3, 4, 5, 8 and 13, Temporal and Drools slides 5, 12 and 13); legacy RWB-E6-019; FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 A1.1, A1.2, A1.4, A2.7, Requirements served and Screens; TSD S7 Write-off and recovery v2 T2, T3.1, T3.2, T3.3, T4, T5.3, T6.1, T8 and T-A; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-16 and R-WO-18; Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-WOF-07
description: (1) decision_reason is the only condition of R-WO-16 and R-WO-18, yet it has no column in write_off (TSD S7 T3.1 lists DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020), no entry in the FSD S7 A2.7.3.2 field catalog (eight write_off fields), no field ID and no list of values; TSD S7 T3.2 publishes no list at all. (2) The decision code the record carries has no value set in any source: the legacy Data table names decision_code as a ledger field and the Business Rules v4 names the event COMMITTEE_REJECTED, but no source publishes the code the reject writes. (3) R-WO-16's owner is 'Case owner' and its systems are 'Committee View, Decision Log', while FSD S7 A2.7.3.3 gives 'Write-off committee member' as the primary role and the legacy permission table gives right A to RW-CREDITAD, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-WOCOMM and RW-FINANCE; TSD S7 T6.1 gives RW-WOCOMM RA, RW-CREDITAD CRUA and the other two RA, so the business role of the rule row and the roles of the permission table do not use the same name. (4) The plan gives H = RWB-S7-E6019-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON with C, I and X empty, while the step reads the rwb-case case, answers the rwb-case case move and reads the rwb-decision package, so three consumed rows have no plan row. (5) DP-04 is absent although the step evaluates the WO route set of 51 rules over 27 states, so no kit row RWB-PLT-E1072-CON or C row RWB-P7-E1073-CON is held. (6) DP-09 is absent although the service owns topic rwb.writeoff.events.v1 with event EV-24, so RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is absent from the H row even though the step needs no outbox. (7) TSD S7 T4 publishes 25 rows and closes at R-WO-25 with 'and 26 more', so no published row moves a case out of RETURNED_TO_PURSUE, the state this story writes. (8) The legacy Data table lists recovery_case and decision_log_entry as the story's entities and rule_row as read, while all three are other services' tables in the target, and it lists no column of write_off, so the reject writes no column of the table and committee_date stays with the approval slice.
evidence: TSD S7 T3.1 field list DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020 with no reason column and T3.2 as an empty list table; FSD S7 A2.7.3.1 rows VR-S7-007-1 and R-WO-16-free, A2.7.3.2 field catalog of the eight write_off fields, A2.7.3.3 roles 'Write-off committee member' primary; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-16 (owner Case owner, systems Committee View and Decision Log) and R-WO-18; TSD S7 T6.1 rights RA for RW-WOCOMM and RW-PRODHEAD, CRUA for RW-CREDITAD, RA for RW-FINANCE; legacy RWB-E6-019 permission table right A for RW-CREDITAD, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-WOCOMM and RW-FINANCE; split plan slice RWB-S7-E6019-APP with three H rows and empty C, I and X; TSD S7 T4 rows R-WO-01 to R-WO-25 and 'and 26 more'; TSD S7 T8 mapping REQ-S7-001 to REQ-S7-008 to FEAT-WOF-01; legacy RWB-E6-019 Data table of recovery_case, decision_log_entry and rule_row
area: Field definition, role mapping, dependency row and state machine
proposed: Keep the plan's H, C, I and X rows as they stand; record the reason and the decision code as request and record inputs with a placeholder until the business lead confirms them; map R-WO-16's owner to the four roles that hold right A in TSD S7 T6.1; declare the three consumed rows in sections 12.2 and 12.8 and record the absent DP-04 and DP-09 rows; leave the onward path of RETURNED_TO_PURSUE to the case owner and raise it in the next planning cut; keep committee_date and every other write_off column out of the reject slice

title: RWB-S7-E6019-CON: the CommitteeDecision and DecisionLogEntry elements, the decision code set, the reason field and the three consumed operation names have no published baseline, and the error set carries no message ID per condition
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S7-E6019-CON; context pack S7 rwb-writeoff; legacy RWB-E6-019; FSD S7 Write-off and recovery v3 A2.7.2, A2.7.3.1, A2.7.3.2, A2.7.4.4 and Screens; TSD S7 Write-off and recovery v2 T2, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.3, T6.1, T8 and T-A.1 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-16 and R-WO-18
description: (1) TSD S7 T-A.2 publishes the request element name CommitteeDecision, the response element name DecisionLogEntry and the error status codes 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, but no property of either element, no required flag, no type and no message ID per condition. (2) No source publishes the decision code set: the legacy Data table names decision_code on decision_log_entry and the rules name the event COMMITTEE_REJECTED, but the value a reject records is not in the FSD, the TSD or the Business Rules and Routing Logic. (3) TSD S7 T3.2 is an empty list-of-values table, so the baseline can publish no enumeration for the decision or the reason, and the reason has neither a length nor a list. (4) No source publishes a REST operation that moves a case state on behalf of a stage, and the S7 row of the connection matrix names Temporal to P7 and P8 with REST and events to P1, so the case move is declared as the child workflow's stage outcome and any REST case-move operation carries a placeholder. (5) TSD S7 T8 maps every REQ-S7 row to FEAT-WOF-01 while the FSD Requirements served table gives REQ-S7-003 as the committee decision of approve, reject or defer, so the contract's requirement trace rests on the FSD row and the TSD map is out of date. (6) The plan's C, I and X rows of this slice are empty while the contract declares three consumed rows.
evidence: TSD S7 T-A.1 operations API-S7-001 and API-S7-002 with request CommitteeDecision and response DecisionLogEntry, T-A.2 error lists 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 without message ids, T3.1 field list of DF-FIN-010 to DF-FIN-020, T3.2 as an empty list table and T8 mapping all eight REQ-S7 rows to FEAT-WOF-01; FSD S7 Requirements served row REQ-S7-003 and A2.7.3.2 field catalog; legacy RWB-E6-019 Data table field decision_code; context pack connection-matrix row S7; split plan slice RWB-S7-E6019-CON with empty H, C, I and X
area: Contract surface, interface names and requirement trace
proposed: Publish the baseline with the placeholders, bind every error condition to one message id of section 14, declare the rejection inside the one published operation and not as a second path, declare the case and package rows as consumed and faked, record the decision-record element and the rights, and trace to REQ-S7-003 on the FSD table until the TSD T8 map is corrected
